pairs.evidence: app/features/settings/billing/billingTypes.ts:84 The billing tab keeps its own hand-copied set of subscription statuses (commented as a MIRROR of the server set in entitlements.ts) to decide checkout vs portal, and billingTypes.test.ts pins it only against status strings typed into the test, never against the server set, so a status added on the server silently forks the client's billing policy.

techniques.evidence: app/features/settings/billing/billingTypes.ts:84 The technique asks for ONE closed status set consumed by every reader, and says a second interpretation elsewhere is a second billing policy. This is a hand-maintained copy with no equality check against SUBSCRIBED_STATUSES in app/_lib/billing/entitlements.ts.

app/features/settings/billing/BillingPlanCatalog.tsx:142 The catalog renders Object.values(data.catalog.plans), which the server serves straight from PLANS. It filters the model instead of copying it, so a new tier shows up without any UI edit.
app/features/settings/billing/BillingPlanCatalog.tsx:54 The label is resolved from the model at render time. Identity comparisons use plan.id (line 147: current={plan.id === data.plan.id}).

app/features/settings/billing/BillingTab.tsx:80 The copy follows the mode. It reads the server's `metered` flag, which meteringActive computes, and on self-hosted installs it hides the current-plan panel and the plan catalog behind BillingSelfHostPanel. No second flag is invented.

pairs.subject: plan-entitlements
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/billing/entitlements.ts:266 The gate answer is a boolean plus one reason: meterGate returns null or a verdict with a single code. So 'not included' (a 0 limit, such as Free's interview_minutes), 'allowance exhausted' and 'balance empty' all come back as the same refusal, and the upgrade prompt cannot tell them apart.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/billing/entitlements.ts:266 The decision is boolean, not the enumerated unlimited/allowance/credit/denied. What works: remaining is returned for batch sizing, and the read and write paths share resolvedLimit and splitSpend. Also, billingOrgForWorkspace (line 37: `?? workspace`) maps a workspace with no org row to its own scope, which then resolves to the free plan with full headroom. The technique calls that a hole and says an unknown tenant should refuse.

app/_lib/billing/price-reconcile.ts:136 PLANS is the single model for limits, labels and display prices, but the plan-to-provider-product binding is hand-listed in several places: this loop, ConfiguredProducts, polar.ts config/productMap (198-200) and the checkout map (306). Adding a tier takes edits in 3+ files, even though the comment at 131 claims a new tier is covered automatically. The model also declares no ordering rank.

app/_lib/billing/price-reconcile.ts:183 A real drift detector exists and runs daily (runPriceReconcile, which records a billing alert), and plans.ts names its prices as display duplicates. But products that could not be fetched are dropped silently instead of being reported in their own 'could not compare' field, a run that compares zero products does not fail, and the comparison is keyed by product, not price id. The technique names all three as failures.

app/_lib/billing/entitlements.ts:64 entitledPlan is one closed status set: past_due/unpaid get a bounded 7-day grace, and canceled keeps the plan through the paid period. reduce.ts and sync.ts add out-of-order guards (a stale revoke, a tombstoned re-entitlement). Pack grants come from the product map, not the payload. clear_subscription leaves the credits balance alone. Missing: rank comparison.

app/_lib/billing/entitlements.ts:213 One shared door, resolvedLimit, is used by both the gate and the debit. The mode is declared once in mode.ts and the default is stated deliberately. mode.test.ts and billing-selfhost.test.ts cover the mode.

app/_lib/billing/plans.ts:34 PlanDef has separate id and name fields, and billing_state stores the id (sync.ts plan: action.plan). The asymmetry (renaming an id is a migration, a label is free) is not stated where the fields are defined.

app/_lib/billing/plans-narrowing.test.ts:41 The catalog lives in code and has an acknowledged baseline of caps. A new cap where there was none counts as a narrowing. Retired tiers stay readable through the `legacy` flag.
app/_lib/billing/plans.ts:117 There are no per-customer commercial records. Enterprise is one shared contact-sales row, and no derived per-customer tier exists to inherit from.
app/_lib/billing/entitlements.ts:175 Limits resolve from the plan alone (plus BYOM's key rule). There is no per-subscription override or removal layer.
app/_lib/billing/enforce.ts:73 Single-repository product: the gate and the meter vocabulary live together, and no entitlement read is served to a third party.
